front.basis: Manual PCB substrate boundary landmarks in the retained high-resolution front photograph; USB overhang excluded. Independent official drawing supplies XY. Height and perspective remain uncalibrated.

review.basis: Independent manufacturer dimension image; affine plane alignment only, no manufactured tolerance claim.

observations: Front, reverse, edge and oblique views inspected; board silhouette, USB direction and component arrangement agree with the retained official views within the declared photo reconstruction scope.
Official dimension-image overlay inspected; nominal board outline, USB, physical RESET, principal packages and header-row placement align by the declared manual affine registration.
Rear UNKNOWN label is visible between the two header rows where present; back layout and component heights remain unverified.
The physical RESET package and cap are visible and do not carry a fabricated GPIO control.
Four sourced mounting holes are open; Nano has no BOOT geometry or control and retains RGB/SCK LED slots 0/1.
Bare variant has open header holes and no pre-soldered header geometry.
limitations: New dimension-photo reconstruction; it does not recover the lost old model bytes or inherit the historical batch-04 visual acceptance.
PCB thickness, component heights, detailed passives, drill metallurgy and connector contact geometry are unmeasured; rear layout and stackup remain visibly UNKNOWN.
Visible RESET has sourced physical geometry but no 3D GPIO control mapping; use the platform restart capability. Nano has no invented BOOT button and GPIO0 remains an RGB channel.
Photo projection shows the visible front appearance only; small raised passives remain flat photographic detail and are not exact mechanical or electrical geometry.
USB is an open approximate metal envelope; tongue, contacts, hole details, insertion depth and cable mating are unverified.
Header body/pin thickness and length are estimates; row count and documented pitch do not establish a physical-fit tolerance.
Original manufacturer source images remain independent references; no real hardware acceptance is claimed.
